title: First sound
learned: Adding modules with the quick search
Turning the rack around with Tab
Patching cables from outputs to inputs
Seeing a wave on the scope

steps.text: Welcome! A modular synth is built from modules. Each module makes or changes a voltage, and cables carry the voltages from module to module. At the end of this lesson you will hear a sound you patched yourself.
First a sound source: an oscillator. Right-click an empty spot in the rack (or press Enter), type VCO and press Enter.
Now an amplifier, the same way: right-click an empty spot, type VCA, press Enter. It will set how loud the sound is.
The jacks of JXMP modules are on the back of the rack, like on real studio gear. Press Tab to turn the rack around.
Drag a cable from SAW of the oscillator to IN 1 of the amplifier. The oscillator now sends its sawtooth wave into the amplifier.
Drag a cable from OUT 1 of the amplifier to jack 1 of the patchbay. The patchbay is the way out of the rack: its front is wired to your speakers. You should hear a buzzing tone now.
Press Tab to turn the rack back to the front, then turn LEVEL 1 of the amplifier. The amplifier sets the volume: down is quiet, up is loud.
Turn the FREQUENCY knob of the oscillator. The frequency is the pitch: how high or low the tone is.
Press Tab and drag a cable from SQR of the oscillator to IN 1 of the amplifier. An input holds one cable, so the old one goes. A square wave sounds hollow, a sawtooth bright.
Now patch SIN to IN 1. The sine is the purest tone, with no overtones at all. The shape of the wave is what you hear as the timbre.
Let's see the wave. Add a scope (type Scope) and drag a second cable from SIN of the oscillator to IN 1 of the scope. One output can feed many inputs.
That's a patch! The oscillator makes the sound, the amplifier sets its volume, and cables carry voltages from outputs to inputs. Press Next to finish.
